story.titleZh: 加里·安德森：红牛与梅赛德斯真正的区别细节
story.summaryZh: 红牛在最近的连续三站赛事中取代了梅赛德斯，成为F1的主导力量。那么，两辆赛车之间的真正区别是什么？

media.altZh: 加里·安德森：红牛与梅赛德斯真正的区别细节 · 第 1 张

story.originalTitle: Gary Anderson: The details that really separate Red Bull and Mercedes
detailZh: 红牛在最近的连续三站赛事中取代了梅赛德斯，成为F1的主导力量。那么，两辆赛车之间的真正区别是什么？
随着F1规则的发展，我常常 wonder 设计和研究领域的成千上万的非常聪明的人可以带来什么新技术到外面的世界。是的，这样的机会一直有限，因为F1汽车上的部件一直太贵，无法直接转移到路上汽车上，但利用它们并证明它们的价值的灵感一直存在。
如果Colin Chapman用他的地面效应汽车，Gordon Murray用他的驾驶员躺下概念，风扇车和加油，或者Derek Gardner用他的六轮Tyrrell，如果他们坐下来准备新赛季，他们会如何看待当前的缺乏创新、严厉、过度规定的规则？
尽管如此，我们仍然看到车队提出的不同之处。没有重大的视觉概念差异，但正如常说的那样，魔鬼在细节中，而这些细节确实带来了收益。
现在，车队们不再追求秒或甚至十分之一秒的进步，而是寻求百分之一秒的提升。对于引入开发套件所付出的所有努力，这样的微小回报很难真正确定你是否取得了进步、停滞不前，或者实际上退步了。
这就是梅赛德斯目前所处的境地。从赛季开始就占据主导地位，并且是遥遥领先的车队，却遭遇了挫折。它在马来西亚引入的开发套件让它感到困惑。是的，数据显示一切都在向积极方向发展，但车手们发现赛车更加难以驾驶，因此也更难从中稳定地提取出圈速。
另一方面，红牛车队却采取了相反的策略。它从自己标准来看几乎灾难性的开局，到占据杆位并赢得最后三场比赛。是的，其中一场是冲刺赛，正如马克斯·维斯塔潘所说，这并不真正算数，但即便如此，这也仅仅表明，在引入开发的时候，任何硬币都有两面，只有一面（或者说一面会）取得成功。
从领先位置开始，让我们比较一下红牛和梅赛德斯。
梅赛德斯和阿斯顿·马丁据我所知是唯一两个在赛季开始时就将前翼安装在第二个元素上的车队（用红色椭圆突出显示）。这意味着在直线模式下，只有第三个元素（橙色高亮箭头）的角度被减小。
总的来说，这个概念可能节省了一些重量，但总的来说，它意味着前翼元素更多地是一个流向优化器，而不是一个主要的下压力产生装置。我这么说是因为第一和第二个元素之间的槽口距离机翼下表面最低气压区域相当近。这个低气压会产生下压力，基本上它会把车拉向赛道。在梅赛德斯的概念中，它将简单地通过那个槽口拉过更多的气流。
我们可以看到，三个元素和弦长度的差异并不大：前翼用浅蓝色箭头突出显示，中间用绿色箭头突出显示，后翼用橙色箭头突出显示。它们的弦长也相当恒定。
红牛、法拉利和麦克拉伦都选择了另一种方法：一个更长的弦长主平面，用深蓝色箭头突出显示。在直线模式下，他们减小了第二个和第三个元素的角度。
我将那根深蓝色的箭头转移到梅赛德斯的前翼上，以展示我对前翼第一元素和第二元素之间缝隙的理解，这个缝隙正好位于其两个前翼元素的总弦长度的中间。
第二和第三元素的弦长，用绿色和橙色箭头突出显示，向外增加。这意味着在船体内部和下方，气流方向变化更少，这里的目的是将最佳和最快的空气质量流引导到地板前缘。
此外，在红牛赛车中，尾翼边缘的细节比梅赛德斯更为复杂。这应该会减少在制动时车辆前部接近地面、在转弯中滚动和转弯出弯时，当翼片的外部部分越过出口边缘时的敏感性。
接下来是地板中央部分的尖端，红牛的地板安装系统（绿色突出显示）基本上将车辆分成两部分。在该安装系统的中间还设置了一个小叶片（紫色突出显示），以帮助整理从前翼中央部分流出的气流。
导流板和地板板区域相似，但实际上在处理它试图管理的气流方面却相当不同。
总的来说，元素的数量相似。然而，红牛似乎在尝试做更多的事情来整理前轮胎的湍流（尾流）。由于F1是一个开放式轮子公式，管理轮胎周围的气流，无论是前轮还是后轮，对于汽车的整体空气动力学性能至关重要。
此外，轮子阻塞可能占汽车阻力的约40%。
当汽车穿过空气时，它必须移除大量的空气。被移除的空气试图填充轮胎后面的空隙，因此管理它并确保它不会对其他产生下压力的设备产生不利影响，基本上就是导流板和地板板区域的作用。红牛正在做更多的事情来尝试在它能够从地板脚板产生下压力之前管理那种湍流，实际上就是地板的前角。
与现在大多数车队所采用的简单下洗侧箱不同，红牛车队保留了抬高的外箱部分，给它带来了一个类似内沟，其侧视图与梅赛德斯侧箱非常相似。
这是为了帮助管理侧箱上的气流并进入变速箱两侧的中央区域，而不是仅仅在油桶区域的整个宽度上产生更多的气流。这样做可以改善扩散器在中央部分最需要改进的地方的性能。
红牛车队似乎在这里实施了一个颇具争议的策略，它有一个非常尖锐的尾缘，红色高光线在这里转为白色。
规则定义了侧箱上角允许的最小半径。大多数车队只是选择这些最小半径，但任何规则都关乎寻找任何灰色地带。通过拥有这个更尖锐的角半径，当来自上侧箱内沟和外侧箱表面的气流汇合时，它将以不同的速度移动，所以基本上沿着那个尖锐的角，它将产生一个涡流，如果正确集中，将沿着后刹车管道的内侧移动，从而在那些刹车管道上安装的转向叶片上产生更高的下压力，进而改善扩散器的性能。
黄色高亮线基本上是梅赛德斯侧箱的侧面轮廓。
我们现在转向后轮胎接触面前面的区域。这同样涉及到管理后轮胎周围的气流，尤其是轮胎接触面区域。
当轮胎在赛道表面上旋转时，你会得到所谓的轮胎喷溅。它既向内又向外。向外，你基本上可以任其自由行动，但向内的轮胎喷溅可能会对扩散器的性能产生不利影响，进而影响整个底板。
这个区域的细节和理念相当相似。红牛的通风系统似乎更靠前，正如你从地板下面的槽口阴影中可以看到的，槽口自然地引导到后轮胎接触面的内侧。
尽管这些是连接地面和车顶的凹槽，但目标实际上是减少从车顶流到底下的溢出物。它们通过将轮胎接触点后方的空腔与轮胎喷射的高能量连接起来，起到密封系统的作用。反过来，通常由于车底低气压而被吸到车底下的气流，现在也被吸到轮胎接触点周围。
扩散器不再是简单的斜坡连接到矩形出口区域的时代已经过去了；现在它是由多个叶片和有策略地放置的开口组成。不想批评梅赛德斯，但红牛的系统似乎在元素细节上更胜一筹。至于梅赛德斯，我还会质疑其内部延伸部分，它将扩散器的后缘连接到翼片，如果可以这么称呼的话，用紫色突出显示。
扩散器的这个内部部分距离来自其他任何组件的气流结构影响最远，因此在这个区域最大化性能可能会很有吸引力。然而，当汽车接近地面或环境温度和/或赛道温度升高时，该区域的气流会变得有些懒散。
当这种情况发生时，很容易诱导气流分离，尤其是在内部垂直表面和扩散器上表面的接合处。
法拉利是第一个引入排气出口斜坡的车队。在许多关于它如何在规定范围内通过其差速器位置实现这一点的讨论之后，其他大多数车队也或多或少地实现了相同的解决方案。基本上，规定要求排气出口的最小尺寸。它必须是圆形的，出口角度也是定义好的，所有这些都是为了减少排气吹拂的可能性。
然而，有志者事竟成。其中一个论点是，规定中没有控制安装支架。无论什么理由，目标都是一样的：在排气出口后面放置某个东西只是将排气流向上方，由于排气出口的一部分被封闭，它增加了其速度。
在全油门和转弯出口时，这两个因素都会改善后翼的尾部下压力，以及我之前提到的那个中央扩散器区域的一致性，该区域之前出现过分离问题。
很多时候我说细节决定成败，所以你可以说，梅赛德斯的双元素叶片应该比红牛的单元素版本要好一些，但在这个案例中，我认为这并不重要。基本上，它是一个改变非常不稳定和湍流排气气流速度和方向的封闭塞，因此添加这个组件做了大部分的工作，优化细节只会带来非常小的回报。
如果我是国际汽联决策小组的一员，我会在一开始就禁止它。理由是，你无法看到所需的开阔空间，它没有达到所需的圆形，并且最后一部分没有在所需的范围内。
坦白地说，我并不是说哪一个方案比另一个更好。得出这个结论需要无数小时的头脑风暴和风洞以及CFD的空气动力学测试。我需要的不仅仅是让我的耳朵分开的东西，而是需要几百（个）其他的贡献。
这主要是为了展示从非常具体的规定中可以产生多大的差异。是的，这些规定不允许你重新发明轮子，但它们仍然允许你在知道什么是最优的，或者希望是最优的之前进行一些思考。
detailEn: Red Bull has taken over from Mercedes as Formula 1’s dominant force, based on what we saw in the recent triple-header. So what’s made the difference between the two cars?

With the way F1 regulations are going, I often wonder what new technologies the thousands of very clever people who work in the design and research areas of these teams can bring to the big world outside. Yes, the opportunity for that has always been limited, as parts on an F1 car have always been much too expensive to transfer directly to road cars, but the inspiration to exploit them and prove their worth has always been there.

What would Colin Chapman with his ground-effect cars, Gordon Murray with his driver-lying-down concept, fan car and refuelling, or Derek Gardner with his six-wheeled Tyrrell think of the current uninventive, draconian, overly-prescriptive regulations if they were sitting down to sharpen their pencils in preparation for the new season?

All that said, we still see differences between what the teams come up with. There are no major visual concept differences, but as is often said, the devil is in the detail, and that detail really does pay dividends.

Now, instead of seconds or even tenths of a second of improvement, the teams are looking for hundredths of a second. With this small return for all the effort of introducing a development package, it is difficult to really be sure if you have moved forward, stood still or actually gone backwards.

This is where Mercedes finds itself at the moment. The dominant team from the start of the season and a runaway championship contender has stumbled. Its development package introduced in Malaysia has confused it. Yes, it says the numbers all add up to a positive, but the drivers are finding the car more difficult and, with that, finding it harder to consistently extract the laptime from it.

On the other hand, Red Bull has done the opposite. It has come from a more or less disastrous start by its standards to be on pole and win the last three races. Yes, one was a sprint, which, as Max Verstappen said, doesn’t really count, but even so, it just shows that when it comes to introducing developments, there are two sides to any coin and only one (or should I say won) will come up trumps.
Starting at the front, let’s compare the Red Bull and Mercedes.

Mercedes and Aston Martin were, as far as I am aware, the only two teams to start the season with the front wing mounted on the second element (highlighted with the red ellipse). This meant that, for straight mode, only the third element (orange highlight arrow) was reduced in angle.

Overall, there is probably a small weight saving with this concept, but in general it has meant that the forward element is more of a flow-direction optimiser as opposed to a major downforce-producing device. I say that because the slot gap between the first and second elements is fairly close to where the lowest air pressure is on the wing’s underside. This low pressure creates downforce, basically it pulls the car towards the track. On the Mercedes concept, it will simply pull more airflow through that slot gap.

We can see here that the chord lengths of the three elements are not vastly different: forward highlighted with the light blue arrow, middle with the green arrow, rear with the orange arrow. They are also fairly constant in chord along their span.

Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren have all gone for the other approach: a much longer-chord mainplane, highlighted with the dark blue arrows. When in straight mode, they reduce the angle of both the second and third elements.

I have transposed that dark blue arrow onto the Mercedes front wing to show what I mean about the slot gap between the forward element and the second element being slap bang in the middle of the total chord length of its two forward elements.

The chord lengths of the second and third elements, highlighted with the green and orange arrows, increase going outwards. This means that there is less airflow direction change inboard and under the chassis, where the objective is to get the best and fastest mass airflow to the leading edge of the underfloor.

Also, on the Red Bull, the detail of the trailing edge of the endplates is more sophisticated than on the Mercedes. This should reduce the sensitivity when the front of the car is close to the ground under braking, in roll mid-corner and on corner exit when the outer part of the wing runs over the exit kerbs.

Moving on to the leading edge of the central section of the floor, the Red Bull floor mounting system (green highlight) basically splits the car into two halves. It also has a small vane (purple highlight) halfway up that mounting system to help tidy up the airflow coming off the central section of the front wing.
The bargeboard and floor plate area is similar but actually fairly different in how it treats the airflow that it is trying to manage.

Overall, there are a similar number of elements. However, Red Bull looks as though it is doing more to attempt to tidy up the front tyre turbulence (wake). F1 being an open-wheel formula, managing the airflow around the tyres, both front and rear, is critical to the car’s overall aerodynamic performance.
Also, the wheel blockage probably accounts for something like 40% of the car’s drag.

As the car passes through the air, it has to displace a serious volume of air. That displaced air tries to fill the void behind the tyres, so managing it and making sure it doesn’t detrimentally affect the other downforce-producing devices is basically what this bargeboard and floor plate area is about. Red Bull is doing more to attempt to manage that turbulence before it does what it can to generate downforce from the floor footplate, in effect the front corner of the floor.

Instead of having a simple downwash sidepod as most teams now have, Red Bull has retained the raised outer section, giving it a gully inboard which is very similar in profile to the Mercedes sidepod in side view.

This is to help manage the airflow over the sidepods and into that central area around the sides of the gearbox, as opposed to just generating more flow through the complete width of the coke bottle area. Doing this can improve the diffuser’s performance where it struggles most, in its central section.
Red Bull also seems to have pulled off something of a controversial coup here, in that it has a very sharp trailing edge where the red highlight line turns to white.

The regulations define the minimum radii allowed on the sidepod’s upper corners. Most teams simply go for those minimum radii but with any regulation, it is about finding any grey areas. By having this sharper corner radius, as the airflow from the upper sidepod gully and the outer sidepod surface joins up, it will be travelling at different speeds, so basically along that sharp corner it will instigate a vortex which concentrated correctly, will travel along the inside of the rear brake ducts, generating higher levels of downforce on the turning vanes that are mounted on those brake ducts and in turn improve the performance of the diffuser.
The yellow highlight line is basically the Mercedes sidepod’s side profile.
We now move on to the area in front of the rear tyre contact patch. This is again about managing the airflow around the rear tyre, especially the tyre’s contact patch area.

As the tyre rotates on the track surface, you get what’s called tyre squirt. It goes both inboard and outboard. Outboard, you can basically let it do what it wants to do, but inboard tyre squirt can be detrimental to the performance of the diffuser and, in turn, the complete underfloor.

The detail and the philosophy in this area are quite similar. The Red Bull vent system seems to be further forward and, as you can see from the slot shadows on the ground below the floor, the slots lead naturally to the inside of the rear tyre contact patch.

Even though these are slots in the floor connecting the top surface to the underside, the objective is to actually reduce the spillage from the top surface going underneath the car. They act like a sealing system by connecting that fairly high-energy tyre squirt to the void behind the tyre’s contact patch. In turn, that airflow that would normally be pulled underneath the car by the low pressure on its underside is also pulled around the tyre contact patch.

Gone are the days when the diffuser was a simple ramp to a rectangular exit area; now it’s a multitude of vanes with strategically placed openings. Not to criticise Mercedes, but the Red Bull system seems to have just that little bit more detail to its elements. The other thing I would question on the Mercedes is the inner extension that connects the trailing edge of the diffuser to the beam wing, if it can be called that, highlighted in purple.

This inner section of the diffuser is furthest away from any influence from airflow structures coming from any other components, and because of that it can be tempting to maximise the performance in that area. However, when the car is close to the ground or the ambient and/or track temperature increases, the airflow in that area gets a bit lazy.
When that happens, it’s very easy to induce airflow separation, especially along the junction of the inner vertical surface and the diffuser’s upper surface.

Ferrari was the first to introduce the exhaust exit ramp. After many column inches about how it had managed this within the regulations only because of its differential position, most of the other teams have achieved more or less the same solution. Basically, the regulations call for an exhaust outlet of a minimum size. It has to be round, and the exit angle is also defined, all of which is to reduce the potential for exhaust blowing.

However, where there is a will, there is a way. One of the arguments was that mounting brackets weren’t controlled in the regulations. Whatever the reasoning, the objective is the same: having something behind the exhaust outlet simply redirects the exhaust flow upwards and, as part of the exhaust outlet is blanked off, it increases its velocity.

On full throttle and at reasonably high revs on corner exit, both of these will improve the rear downforce from the rear wing and consistency in that central section of the diffuser that I spoke about suffering from separation problems earlier.

Many times I say the devil is in the detail, so I suppose you could say that the twin element vane on the Mercedes should be a little better than the single element version on the Red Bull, but in this case I don’t think it really matters. Basically, it is a blanking plug that alters the velocity and direction of the very inconsistent and turbulent exhaust gas flow, so adding the component does most of the heavy lifting and optimising the detail would give a very small return.

If I were part of the decision-making group at the FIA, I would have banned it from day one. The reasoning would be that you couldn’t see the required opening, it wasn’t round as required, and the last section wasn’t within the required angle.

To be honest and upfront, I’m not saying either package is better than the other. To reach that conclusion would require countless hours of head-scratching and aerodynamic testing in both the windtunnel and CFD. Instead of just what keeps my ears apart, I would need a few (hundred) others to contribute.

This is mainly to show just what differences you can get from a very prescriptive set of regulations. Yes, those regulations don’t allow you to reinvent the wheel, but they still allow for some grey-matter scratching before you know what’s best, or hopefully best.

relatedItems.summaryZh: 法拉利在美国大奖赛的最后一场练习赛中完成了全部的顶尖成绩，尽管查尔斯·勒克莱尔因超车限界被删除成绩，但最终是刘易斯·汉密尔顿位居第一。
relatedItems.originalTitle: Ferrari completes US GP practice sweep
detailZh: 法拉利在奥斯汀的最终练习赛中完成了美国大奖赛的一整套顶尖F1练习时间，尽管查尔斯·勒克莱尔因为超车限界被扣除时间，这次是刘易斯·汉密尔顿位居第一。
周五的领跑者勒克莱尔失去了比汉密尔顿快0.083秒的时间，因此跌至第三，排在马克斯·维斯塔潘之后，因为他不得不依靠中胎时间。
在车队转向排位赛模拟之前，法拉利在练习赛的第一部分的长距离跑中也一直处于领先地位。
汉密尔顿对加布里埃尔·博尔特莱托在练习赛中发生的交通事件表示了不满——这是当节练习中众多事件之一， stewards 将会对此进行调查。
勒克莱尔并非唯一违反赛道的车手，整个练习赛中， 删除，指因违反规则而取消圈速的数量惊人。车手积分榜领跑者基米·安东内利和两位麦克拉伦车手也成为了其他引人注目的违规者。
勒克莱尔的圈速损失意味着红牛车队以维斯塔潘的成绩结束练习赛，排在第二位，他和伊萨克·哈德贾在车队无线电中（亚历克斯·阿隆索也受到了哈德贾的指责）有很多抱怨，维斯塔潘在练习赛结束时经历了一次疯狂的锁死、滑动和打滑。
安东内利最终排在第四位，领先于他的梅赛德斯车队队友乔治·拉塞尔。
圈速删除帮助尼克·胡肯伯格将奥迪车队提升至第七位，分开了两辆麦克拉伦赛车。

detailEn: Ferrari completed a full set of top United States Grand Prix Formula 1 practice times in the final session at Austin, though a track limits deletion for Charles Leclerc meant this time it was Lewis Hamilton on top.
Friday pacesetter Leclerc lost a time that had been 0.083 seconds faster than Hamilton, falling to third behind Max Verstappen as a result as he had to rely on a medium-tyre time.
Ferrari had also been on top during the longer runs in the first part of the session before teams switched to qualifying simulations.
Hamilton expressed his frustration with Gabriel Bortoleto over a traffic incident - one of quite a few in the session - that will be looked at by the stewards.

Leclerc was far from the only driver to fall foul of track limits as the wild number of laptime deletions continued through the session. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli and both McLaren drivers were among the other high-profile transgressors.

Though Leclerc's lap loss meant Red Bull ended the session second with Verstappen, both he and Isack Hadjar had plenty of complaints over team radio (with Alex Albon also getting Hadjar's ire) and Verstappen having a wild lock-up, slide and wheelspin moment to end his session.
Antonelli ended up fourth ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell.
The laptime deletions helped Nico Hulkenberg to get Audi as high as seventh, splitting the McLarens.
12 Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) +1.188s
16 Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin) +1.562s

法拉利在练习赛的前半段表现优异。
勒克莱尔对交通事件表示不满， stewards 将对此进行调查。
keyPointsEn: Leclerc's lap time was deleted due to track limits, with Hamilton taking the top spot by 0.083 seconds.
Ferrari had a strong performance in the first part of the session.
Leclerc expressed frustration over a traffic incident that stewards will investigate.

relatedItems.titleZh: 赫塔或于2027年取代博塔斯加盟凯迪拉克
relatedItems.summaryZh: 凯迪拉克2027年F1车手阵容尚未确定，储备车手科尔顿·赫塔是可能取代瓦尔特利·博塔斯的人选之一。车队领队马尔钦·布德科夫斯基在奥斯汀表示，车手合同不会在新闻发布会上讨论。
relatedItems.originalTitle: Herta could replace Bottas at Cadillac in F1 2027
relatedItems.summaryEn: Cadillac's 2027 Formula 1 driver line-up is not yet finalised, with reserve driver Colton Herta among those in contention to replace Valtteri Bottas. Team boss Marcin Budkowski said in Austin that driver contracts are not something discussed in the press.
detailZh: 凯迪拉克2027年F1车手阵容尚未确定，储备车手科尔顿·赫塔是可能取代瓦尔特利·博塔斯的人选之一。
博塔斯和塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯都以长期合同加入F1 2026年新军凯迪拉克，但The Race了解到，车队尚未就明年由谁驾驶做出最终决定。
在周五的奥斯汀新闻发布会上，被问及佩雷斯和博塔斯是否会留队至2027年时，凯迪拉克车队领队马尔钦·布德科夫斯基没有排除这种可能。
“这是我最不可能评论车手合同的地方，总的来说，我认为这不是在新闻发布会上做的事，”布德科夫斯基说。
“这件事会在时机成熟时由车队通过官方发布来完成。”
凯迪拉克必须在两种选择之间做出决定：是保持连续性，继续沿用两位熟悉冠军车队运作的资深车手，还是认为现在正是做出改变、为未来争取更大潜在收益的合适时机。
没有任何迹象表明佩雷兹有失去席位的风险，因为今年他一直是凯迪拉克表现更强的车手，并在幕后大力推动车队改进。
今年排位赛中，博塔斯和佩雷兹实力相当接近，佩雷兹以13比9领先博塔斯，但在正赛中佩雷兹拥有明显优势。在两人同时于赛道上的比赛圈数中，博塔斯仅有18%的时间领先于佩雷兹。
博塔斯也经历了一些特别艰难的大奖赛，包括上一场在新加坡的比赛，他在那里的圈速比佩雷兹慢了约1.5秒，且没有明确的解释。
这意味着他在2027年的席位存疑，26岁的赫塔是可能取代他的人选之一。
为什么“令人失望”的F2赛季没有损害赫塔的机会
赫塔今年从印地赛车转投二级方程式，明确目标就是进入F1——2023年他曾非常接近红牛青训车队的位置。
赫塔自称他在F2的赛季表现“令人失望”，在22名全职车手中排名第19位，而赛季还剩卡塔尔和阿布扎比两站。
“对我来说，也许问题比答案多，也许进入这个赛季时问题更多，所以我对这方面的一切都相当失望，”赫塔在奥斯汀说。
“我只是对今年的进展感到失望；一点都不好。”
赫塔明年不太可能留在F2再跑一个赛季，但他已经明确表示，他仍然希望明年能有某种形式的比赛计划，而F1仍然是最终目标。
凯迪拉克并未因赫塔在F2令人失望的表现而退缩，因为它知道完成这一转变会很困难，并且对赫塔在其F1赛车中所做的工作印象深刻。
然而，这确实意味着赫塔的锦标赛最终排名几乎肯定无法为他赢得任何来自F2的超级驾照积分，但凯迪拉克正在确保他将达到40分的门槛。
周五在奥斯汀，赫塔参加了今年第四次第一节自由练习，但其中只有三次有资格获得超级驾照奖励积分，因为蒙扎的一次技术问题意味着他没有完成获得超级驾照积分所需的100公里运行里程。
这一点，加上他在印地赛车中的成绩——包括2024年获得亚军、仅次于冠军亚历克斯·帕劳的30分——意味着他现在距离门槛只差一分。
The Race 了解到，赫塔将在年底前再参加一次第一节练习赛，以确保他达到 40 分，从而成为 2027 年的一个选项。
赫塔还在赛道之外完成了私人的 F1 测试，作为 阿尔派 车队旧车测试（TPC）项目的一部分在波尔蒂芒驾驶，他驾驶的是地面效应时代的赛车。
凯迪拉克没有自己的旧车测试（TPC）项目，因此，就像 2025 年底让佩雷兹驾驶旧法拉利一样，它已与一支竞争对手车队达成协议，以确保赫塔获得更多里程。
自从最初以安德雷蒂的名义争取 F1 参赛资格以来，凯迪拉克一直表示，如果有美国车手能凭实力赢得席位，它希望拥有这样一位车手，而赫塔是最合乎逻辑的候选人。
其他竞争者？
赫塔并非博塔斯席位的唯一竞争者，因为多位车手一直在联系凯迪拉克——这是唯一“开放”的席位，而小红牛只在红牛签约车手之间做选择。
埃斯特班·奥康在输给法拉利青训车手拉斐尔·卡马拉后，正寻求明年留在F1发车区的方法，但The Race了解到他不会以正赛车手或储备车手的身份加入凯迪拉克。
相反，他很可能在另一支车队担任储备车手，例如阿斯顿·马丁。
红牛储备车手角田裕毅在今年早些时候意外代表小红牛出战三场比赛后，正寻求永久重返发车格。
角田裕毅的经纪人已就2027年的机会与凯迪拉克接触，他是候选人之一。
凯迪拉克并不急于做出最终决定，因为其他候选人目前都没有其他车队正式车手席位的机会。
如果凯迪拉克选择在2027年替换博塔斯，鉴于博塔斯与车队有长期合同，双方需要达成某种安排。
detailEn: Cadillac's 2027 Formula 1 driver line-up isn't yet finalised, with reserve driver Colton Herta among those in contention to replace Valtteri Bottas.
Both Bottas and Sergio Perez joined F1's 2026 new team Cadillac on long-term deals, but The Race understands the team hasn't made a final decision on who will drive for it next year.
In the Austin press conference on Friday, Cadillac team boss Marcin Budkowski left the door open when asked if Perez and Bottas will stay on for 2027.
"This is the last place I would comment on driver contracts, and in general, I think it's not something that is done in the press," Budkowski said.
"It's something which will be done by official releases from the team when the time is right."

Cadillac has to decide between sticking with the continuity of its two experienced drivers with knowledge of championship-winning teams or whether it's the right time to make a change with potentially bigger upsides for the future.
There's nothing to suggest Perez is at risk of losing his seat, as he's been the stronger Cadillac driver this year and has pushed the team hard behind-the-scenes to improve.

Bottas and Perez have been fairly evenly matched in qualifying this year, with Perez leading Bottas 13-9, but it's in the races where Perez has had a clear margin. Bottas has only spent 18% of the racing laps they've both been on track ahead of Perez.
Bottas has also had some particularly tough grands prix, including the last race in Singapore, where he was lapping around 1.5 seconds slower than Perez without a clear explanation.
That means his seat is in doubt for 2027, with 26-year-old Herta among those who could replace him.
Why "disappointing" F2 season hasn't hurt Herta's chances
Herta swapped IndyCar for Formula 2 this year with the specific aim of reaching F1 - something he came very close to with Red Bull's junior team in 2023.
Herta has had a self-described "disappointing" F2 campaign as he's 19th out of 22 full-time drivers with two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi remaining.
"Maybe a few more questions than answers for me, maybe more questions than going into it, so I'm fairly disappointed with everything on that side of things," Herta said at Austin.
"I'm just disappointed with how the year's gone; it's not been good at all."
It's unlikely Herta will stay in F2 for a second season next year, but he's made it clear he'd still like a racing programme of some kind next year, with F1 still the ultimate goal.
Cadillac isn't put off by Herta's disappointing F2 performances as it knew making the switch would be difficult, and it's been impressed by the work Herta has done in its F1 car.
It does mean, however, that Herta's championship finish is all but certain not to earn him any superlicence points from F2, but Cadillac is ensuring he'll reach the 40-point threshold.

Herta took part in his fourth FP1 of the year at Austin on Friday, but only three of those are eligible for the superlicence bonus point, as a technical issue at Monza meant he didn't clear the 100km of running necessary to gain the superlicence point.
That, added together with his IndyCar results - including 30 points for finishing runner-up to champion Alex Palou in 2024 - means he's now one point away from the threshold.
The Race understands Herta will do another FP1 before the end of the year to make sure he gets to 40 points so he can be an option for 2027.

Herta has also completed private F1 testing away from the circuit, having run in an Alpine as part of that team's Testing of Previous Cars programme at Portimao, where he ran in a ground effect-era car.
Cadillac doesn't have a TPC programme of its own, so, just as when it ran Perez in an old Ferrari in late 2025, it's struck a deal with a rival team to ensure Herta gets more mileage.
Since first gunning for an F1 entry under the Andretti banner, Cadillac has long stated its ambition to have an American driver if one can earn a seat on merit with Herta the most logical candidate.
Other contenders?
Herta isn't the only contender for Bottas's seat, as multiple drivers have been contacting Cadillac - it's the only ‘open' seat, with Racing Bulls only picking between Red Bull-contracted drivers.

Esteban Ocon is looking for a way to stay on the F1 grid next year after losing his seat to Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, but The Race understands he won't be joining Cadillac in a race or reserve driver role.
Instead, he's likely to take a reserve driver role at a different team such as Aston Martin.
Red Bull reserve driver Yuki Tsunoda is looking for a permanent return to the grid after his unexpected three-race return with Racing Bulls earlier this year.
Tsunoda's representatives have been contacting Cadillac over a 2027 opportunity and he is among the contenders.
Cadillac isn't in a rush to make a final decision, as none of the candidates have race seat options elsewhere.
Should it elect to replace Bottas for 2027, it would need to come to some kind of arrangement given he has a long-term deal with the team.
keyPointsZh: 博塔斯和塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯都以长期合同加入凯迪拉克，但车队尚未就明年由谁驾驶做出最终决定。
布德科夫斯基表示，车手合同事宜将在合适时机由车队官方发布。
佩雷斯今年是凯迪拉克表现更强的车手，排位赛以13比9领先博塔斯，正赛优势更为明显。
keyPointsEn: Both Bottas and Sergio Perez joined Cadillac on long-term deals, but the team has not made a final decision on who will drive for it next year.
Budkowski said driver contract matters will be handled through official team releases when the time is right.
Perez has been the stronger Cadillac driver this year, leading Bottas 13-9 in qualifying with a clearer margin in races.

relatedItems.titleZh: 法拉利2026年最后重大F1升级解析
relatedItems.summaryZh: 法拉利带来其2026年最后的F1赛车更新，虽然改动不大，但累积起来效果显著。法拉利在性能上并未落后太多，但执行和决策失误导致丢分。

media.altZh: 法拉利2026年最后重大F1升级解析 · 第 1 张

relatedItems.originalTitle: Ferrari's last major 2026 F1 upgrade explained
detailZh: 法拉利带来其2026年最后的F1赛车更新。
从我们所能看到的，这并不是一个巨大的变化 - 只是各个区域细节上的小改动，但正如我经常说的，它们都会累积起来。
说实话，法拉利在性能上并没有落后太多。它是因为执行和决策失误而丢分。我知道刘易斯·汉密尔顿在新加坡VSC下没有进站，这就是法拉利决策失误导致丢分的例子之一。
毫无疑问，汉密尔顿在做出进站决策方面有很多经验 - 有好有坏 - 但我对车手越权团队的做法表示担忧，因为任何车手，他们只有自己的信息，最多也就是前后的车辆信息，关于轮胎情况。团队应该有 - 或者至少应该有 - 所有仍在运行的车辆的信息，因此对发生的事情有一个更全面的了解，所以它应该能够做出更好的决策。
我说‘应该’是因为我不知道法拉利是否只关注自己的赛车，而且似乎有人不愿意冒险出头。如果你不做决定，你就永远不会因为做出错误的决定而承担责任。
法拉利也因为不允许最快的车手继续前进而丢掉了很多积分——这又回到了决策的应变性。
无论如何，这是我今天的抱怨——接下来是发展。正如我所说，从我所能看到的，这只是细节上的小变化。
紫色鳍将散热器进气口与油箱底部的导流板分离，似乎尺寸略有增加。随着车速的增加，散热器将无法流动出它所面对的空气量——当这种情况发生时，进气道将开始溢出到车身外表面。这个鳍将减少这种溢出对底座侧箱的不利影响。
实际上，这意味着地板脚翼叶片（导流板）将表现出更高的稳定性。
至于侧箱，整体轮廓有所改变。上表面现在在后方更低，导致更多的下洗气流覆盖该表面。这意味着侧箱在尾缘的体积已经减少，从而在后刹车通风口内侧和车身内表面之间打开了油桶形状的区域。
此外，位于CEVA标志下方的小型提前进站似乎也增加了深度。这些车身轮廓的小幅变化减少了呈现在地板下方外边缘的气流量——该区域的气流将被汽车下方的低压区域吸到地板下方，进而减少地板下方的整体下压力。
与侧箱入口和侧箱本身的改变相辅相成的是扩散器区域的创新。在外上尾缘角落，法拉利从简单的格尼翼（用绿色突出显示）转变为更复杂的叶片（用紫色突出显示）。这个外角是可能遭受气流分离问题的一个区域。新的叶片将其与安装在后刹车通风口内表面的多个转向叶片连接起来。
法拉利也对扩散器叶片进行了改动（蓝色部分突出）。可能还有更多的改动，但最明显的是对下尾翼角落的不同处理——这个新细节应该会在现在90°的尾部角落产生涡流，甚至可能是两个涡流。如果是这样，这将有助于将扩散器与赛道表面密封，从而提高其内侧扩散器的性能。
当你试图更努力地工作扩散器和底盘时，任何类似这样的改动都很容易增加对赛道表面的敏感性，从而导致尖锐的下压力。然而，在奥斯汀，由于崎岖的赛道表面，法拉利可能会将赛车调得稍微软一点，并且因此，高出一毫米或两毫米。对于可能遇到相同问题的其他车队也是如此——因此，梅赛德斯可能能够从其在马来西亚（巴林）引入的更新中获得更好的性能。
总的来说，看到至少四支车队和八名车手相互竞争是非常令人高兴的，这就是赛车应该有的样子——而且，作为一个小型车队，看到小红牛让这四支大型车队保持诚实也是一件好事。
detailEn: Ferrari has arrived in Austin with what should be its last Formula 1 car update of 2026.
From what we can see, it’s not a massive change - just small changes to the details in various areas, but as I often say, they all add up.

To be honest, Ferrari has not been that far behind as far as performance is concerned. It's been points lost through execution and decision-making. I know that Lewis Hamilton put his hand up as to not pitting under the VSC in Singapore, for instance, but that’s just one example of Ferrari's indecisions costing it.

Without doubt, Hamilton has lots of experience when it comes to making pit calls - some good, some bad - but my concern with the driver overruling the team is that for any driver, they only have their own information, and at most that of the cars in front and behind them, as to what the tyre situation is. The team has - or at least should have - the information from all of the cars still running, so a much broader picture of what is happening, so it should be able to make a better decision.

I say 'should' here because I have no idea if Ferrari looks any further than its own cars and also there seems to be a bit of a reluctance for anyone to put their heads above the parapet. If you don’t make decisions, you can never be held responsible for making the wrong decision.
Ferrari has also thrown away quite a few points by not allowing whatever driver is fastest to just press on - again, that falls into the reactiveness of decision making.
Anyway, that’s my moan for today - onto the developments. As I said, from what I can see, it is small detail changes.

The purple fin separating the radiator intake from the coke bottle undercut seems to have increased in size slightly. As the car speed increases, the radiator will not be able to flow the volume of air that is presented to it - when this happens, the inlet duct will start to spill around the outer body surface. This fin will reduce the adverse effect this spillage would have on the undercut sidepod.
In reality, it means that the floor foot vanes (bargeboards) will perform more consistently.

As for the sidepods, there's a change to the overall profile. The upper surface is now lower at the rear, inducing more downwash over that upper surface. This means that the sidepod's volume at its trailing edge has been reduced, opening up the coke bottle section between the inside of the rear brake duct and the inner body surface.

Also, the small undercut below the CEVA decal looks like it has also been increased in depth. These small changes in body profile reduce the amount of airflow that is presented to the outer edge of the underfloor - airflow in that area will be pulled under the underfloor by the low pressure underneath the car, and in turn that will reduce the overall downforce produced by the underfloor.

To go hand in hand with the changes at the sidepod inlet and the sidepod itself are novelties in the diffuser area. On the outer upper trailing edge corner, Ferrari has gone from a simple gurney flap (highlighted in green) to a more sophisticated vane (highlighted in purple). This outer corner is one area that can suffer from airflow separation problems. The new vane connects it to the multiple turning vanes mounted on the inner surface of the rear brake ducts.

Ferrari has also introduced changes to the diffuser vanes (highlighted in blue). There are probably further changes, but the obvious is the different trim to the lower trailing edge corner - this new detail should instigate a vortex, perhaps even two vortices, coming off that now-90° rear corner. If so, this will help seal that splitter to the track surface, improving the performance of the actual diffuser inboard of them.

Anything like this, when you are attempting to work the diffuser and underfloor harder, can very easily increase sensitivity to the track surface so lead to pointy downforce. However, in Austin, because of the bumpy track surface, Ferrari will probably be running the car just that little bit softer and, with that, a millimetre or two higher. The same is true for other teams that might be suffering from the same problems - so Mercedes might be able to get a better performance from its updates introduced in Malaysia (Bahrain).

Overall, it’s great to see at least four teams and eight drivers battling with each other, that’s what racing should be about - on top of that, as a small team, it is good to see Racing Bulls keeping those four big teams honest.
